title: Recovered — claims that computed and were withdrawn for want of a proof — 15 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Recovered — claims that computed and were withdrawn for want of a proof. 15 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/recovered.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 3 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 43 pairs; the theorems fall into 6 strands, the largest of 9. Most binding: units (7), pow9 (7), triad (2). 4 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/recovered.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 15 sealed receipts fold to 31d07f8b-f421-81f8-a182-748948c44492. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 6, 1, 2, 8, 5, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: theorems.lean (4 observed, 1.24 expected, lift 3.24), generated.lean (6 observed, 2.01 expected, lift 2.99), demand3.lean (4 observed, 2.16 expected, lift 1.85). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.78 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 34.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.79; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.51. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 7b6f6e8d1e91 (2026-09-15), over 681 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Every fact here is standard: the units of ℤ/9 are {1,2,4,5,7,8}, their product is −1 (Wilson), 2 generates them with order 6, and the Pisano period of Fibonacci mod 9 is 24. Textbook material, credited. What is NOT prior art is that these particular statements sat WITHDRAWN in this deposit's ledger, each recorded as "not backed by a Lean proof. Its evidence is a TypeScript test", while every one is decidable in a line. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. units_sum_zero — (units.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 27 ∧ (units.foldl (· + ·) 0) % 9 = 0 record
  2. self_inverse_1_8 — ((List.range 9).filter (fun d => d * d % 9 == 1)) = [1, 8] record
  3. triad_nilpotent — triad.all (fun d => d * d % 9 == 0) record
  4. triad_sum_zero — (triad.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 18 ∧ (triad.foldl (· + ·) 0) % 9 = 0 record
  5. units_product_neg1 — (units.foldl (· * ·) 1) % 9 = 8 record
  6. order_of_2_is_6 — pow9 2 6 = 1 ∧ ((List.range' 1 5).all (fun k => pow9 2 k != 1)) record
  7. sum_1_to_9_zero — ((List.range' 1 9).foldl (· + ·) 0) = 45 ∧ ((List.range' 1 9).foldl (· + ·) 0) % 9 = 0 record
  8. doubling_digitroot_period6 — ((List.range 6).map (fun k => pow9 2 k)) = [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5] ∧ pow9 2 6 = pow9 2 0 record
  9. unit_exp_id_k6 — units.all (fun u => pow9 u 6 == 1) record
  10. unit_exp_id_k12 — units.all (fun u => pow9 u 12 == 1) record
  11. unit_exp_id_k18 — units.all (fun u => pow9 u 18 == 1) record
  12. powperm_k5 — (units.map (fun u => pow9 u 5)).eraseDups.length = 6 record
  13. powperm_k7 — (units.map (fun u => pow9 u 7)).eraseDups.length = 6 record
  14. qr_u1 — (List.range 9).any (fun d => d * d % 9 == 1) record
  15. qr_u4 — (List.range 9).any (fun d => d * d % 9 == 4) record
